newsitem.title: IRAQ: IRAQ STARTS PUMPING OIL THROUGH PIPELINE TO TURKEY.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ STARTS PUMPING OIL THROUGH PIPELINE TO TURKEY.

text.p: Iraq resumed pumping oil through the Iraq-Turkish pipeline to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan early on Thursday, an Iraqi oil ministry source said.
"Around 2.00 a.m. early today oil pumping from Kirkuk (in northern Iraq) to the Turkish port of Ceyhan has started," the source told Reuters.
The source said nearly six million barrels of Iraqi crude were currently in storage tanks at Ceyhan.
The resumption of pumping coincides with oil being loaded onto tankers at Ceyhan.
The first tanker began loading from Ceyhan at 2100 GMT on Wednesday, a Turkish pipeline official said.
"The lifting will take 39 hours, it started at midnight (2100 GMT). A total of 290,986 tonnes will be loaded in 39 hours.
"Its destination is the United States," Murat Demir, an official at the state pipeline company Botas, told Reuters.
